rules.notes: A person's identity is not replaced by a name form. A book or user profile may deliberately choose a reviewed local equivalent, adaptation, or transliteration.
Teach the distinction between preserving a name in another script/sound system and choosing a historically related local equivalent.
George/Jorge-style relationships can reveal shared name history without claiming every culturally related form is interchangeable in every context.

Culture notes may include reviewed examples such as Chinese adaptation/transliteration strategies and Deaf-community name-sign practices. These require sourced cultural notes, not generalization from one language to another.
If the learner supplies a name, search the reviewed name database. Unknown names remain usable as entered and create a research request rather than an invented equivalence.

triggers.notes: Any resolved name tap may expose a compact names-vary-across-languages footnote and offer this lesson. The tap must not interrupt reading automatically.
A queued conversational knot may invite the learner to explore their name after they provide it.
A names-focused book or chapter can advertise this topic and offer the lesson even if onboarding skipped it.

interaction_defaults.dismissal_behavior: Never force the lesson. Name taps may offer Learn now or Queue lesson; dismissal leaves the story uninterrupted.
interaction_defaults.cooldown_policy: The compact name primer may be shown for a small bounded number of early name taps, then collapse by default; the lesson remains manually available.
